current.text: He was traded to Toronto and takes Brandon Ingram's spot. He faces no punishment from the league ruling, and the trade is expected to go through.
He is a projected starter and part of the expected closing five, with Quickley, Barrett, Barnes and Poeltl or Murray-Boyles.
Much of the Toronto offense is expected to run through him, with usage moving away from Barrett and Quickley. His numbers should stay close to last season's.
He is coming off one of his best and healthiest seasons in years.
He is expected to miss time this season. Sean projects about 60 to 65 games.
The Raptors have 15 back-to-backs, three of them in the fantasy playoffs.
He is expected to play some back-to-backs but not all. Josh expects load management in Toronto.
Per game he is a top 5 to top 10 player, with a tight range: best case 4th, worst case about 21st.
Experts call his ADP of about 20 to 30 too high. They would not take him inside the top 40 in head-to-head because of injury risk. He is fair value from about pick 41 or round 5.

durable.text: He has a degenerative knee condition with repeated surgeries in the same knee: meniscus, ACL and quad tendinopathy. He also carries ankle sprain risk.
Experts do not trust his knee to hold up. Their main worry is injuries and load management.
He is a high-usage scorer, with usage above 30 percent. He is a good and willing three-point shooter who makes decisions quickly.
He is one of the best free throw shooters in recent memory.
Steals are his standout category, far above the pool. He is also strong in points and FT% and has no weak category.
As an often-injured player, he is worth taking a bit earlier in roto than in head-to-head.

note: Per game he is a top 10 player who fits every build, with standout steals and strong points and FT%. The experts agree the knee and load management make him a pick from about 41st onward in H2H, not at his ADP of 20 to 30. Prices range from 25 USD (Yahoo value) to 42 USD (ESPN value), and he went for 20 USD in our league last season, so bid in the low to mid 20s and let someone else pay ESPN prices. Early in the season, watch how many of Toronto's 15 back-to-backs he plays, because three fall in our playoff weeks.
